name: Ganoderma lingzhi

size_cm.source: Wang, Xi, Li, Wang & Yao 2012, The species identity of the widely cultivated Ganoderma, 'G. lucidum' (Ling-zhi), in China, PLoS ONE 7(7):e40857
size_cm.note: pileus 3.0-14.5 x 6.0-15.5 cm in the description of the cultivated Chinese Ling-zhi, which that paper calls G. sichuanense; the same fungus was named G. lingzhi by Cao, Wu & Dai 2012 and the synonymy is disputed

notes: One file for the G. lingzhi / G. lucidum group, whose species limits are disputed. Reported (unchecked) to be cultivated, to have a sequenced genome, to grow as antlers in high CO2 and to be used in mycelium materials; the related G. resinaceum has spikes 5 to 8 min wide [10].

spike_interval.note: Ganoderma resinaceum fruit bodies, not this species: two spike trains had mean intervals of 731 s and 2300 s (12 and 38 min); 25 min is the middle of the two. A fast burst had 92 s spacing. Adamatzky & Gandia 2021, On electrical spiking of Ganoderma resinaceum, bioRxiv 2021.06.18.449000, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.06.18.449000.full

spike_duration.note: Ganoderma resinaceum fruit bodies, not this species: most common spike width 300 to 500 s, given as 5 to 8 min; middle taken. Adamatzky & Gandia 2021, On electrical spiking of Ganoderma resinaceum, bioRxiv 2021.06.18.449000, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.06.18.449000.full

spike_amplitude.note: Ganoderma resinaceum fruit bodies, not this species: most common amplitudes 0.1 to 0.4 mV, extracellular needle electrodes 1 to 2 cm apart; middle taken. Adamatzky & Gandia 2021, On electrical spiking of Ganoderma resinaceum, bioRxiv 2021.06.18.449000, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.06.18.449000.full

tip_speed.note: 7.8 mm/day at the 30 to 34 C optimum for North American 'G. lucidum' isolates (Adaskaveg & Gilbertson 1986, Mycologia 78:694-705, https://doi.org/10.1080/00275514.1986.12025312); x 41.7 = 325 um/h. Read from a search snippet of the abstract: the publisher page refused the fetch. Not the Asian lingzhi itself. Korean strains reached 87 mm colony diameter in 10 days at 30 C on 90 mm PDA plates (Jayasinghe et al. 2008, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3755248/), a plate-limited lower bound of about 4 mm/day radial

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Jayasinghe, Imtiaj, Hur, Lee, Lee & Lee 2008, Favorable culture conditions for mycelial growth of Korean wild strains in Ganoderma lucidum, Mycobiology 36(1):28-33
t_opt.note: ten Korean wild strains on PDA, 15 to 35 C in 5 C steps, 10 days: best growth at 30 C, favourable range 25 to 30 C; four strains did best at 25 C. Two strains did not grow at 15 C and three did not grow at 35 C, so the limits vary by strain and are left at the family default
